results.title: a. Are there “hypergeometric sampling plans”? A sampling plan should specify the sample size (or a procedure for stopping the sampling if results on the sampled items up to that point make further testing unnecessary). For sampling a finite population without replacement, the hypergeometric probability distribution applies to sample-size computations. But how does that make the sampling plan hypergeometric? The simplest “plan,” one would think, is to take a random sample of a size determined in light of the sample-size as computed with the hypergeometric distribution. The result is just a simple random sample.
